Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 56 s. 2023 SEP 04 MS. MA. BELEN PAURA mabelpaural 102@gmail.com Dear Ms. Paura: This has reference to your electronic mail requesting this Department's opinion on whether the Punong Barangay's attendance to the session virtually is allowed. Per your representation, your Punong Barangay fails to perform his duties due to his medical condition. He is sick, and was not able to file corresponding leave of absence, however, he is attending sessions virtually. Thus, there has been paralysis of the transactions of the Barangay as the Punong Barangay cannot sign/approve the necessary documents. At the outset, the query on whether an online session is allowed was already answered by the Department in its Legal Opinion No. 50, series of 2020. It categorically states: In reply to the second query, again, there is no law, rules and regulations, even RA 11469 or the Bayanihan to Heal as One Act which was passes primarily to address the Covid-19 pandemic and the Presidential decrees issued by the Office of the President, which authorize the local sanggunians to conduct sessions through teleconferencing, video conferencing and other electronic means. Due to the absence of any law, rules and regulations, the following provisions of the LGC still govern the conduct of sanggunian sessions, to wit: SECTION 52. Sessions. - (a) On the first day of the session immediately following the election of its members, the Sanggunian shall, by resolution, fix the day, time, and place of its regular sessions. The minimum number of regular sessions shall be once a week for the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Panlungsod, and Sangguniang bayan, and twice a month for the Sangguniang Barangay. (b) When public interest so demands, special sessions may be called by the local chief executive or by a majority of the members of the Sanggunian. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

(c) All Sanggunian sessions shall be open to the public unless a closed- door session is ordered by an affirmative vote of a majority of the members present, there being a quorum, in the public interest or for reasons of security, decency, or morality. No two (2) sessions, regular or special, may be held in a single day. (d) In the case of special sessions of the Sanggunian, a written notice to the members shall be served personally at the member's usual place of residence at least twenty- four (24) hours before the special session is held. Unless otherwise concurred in by two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Sanggunian members present, there being a quorum, no other matters may be considered at a special session except those stated in the notice. (e) Each Sanggunian shall keep a journal and record of its proceedings which may be published upon resolution of the Sanggunian concerned. SECTION 53. Quorum. - (a) A majority of all the members of the Sanggunian who have been elected and qualified shall constitute a quorum to transact 30 official business. Should a question of quorum be raised during a session, the presiding officer shall immediately proceed to call the roll of the members and thereafter announce the results. (b) Where there is no quorum, the presiding officer may declare a recess until such time as a quorum is constituted, or a majority of the members present may adjourn from day to day and may compel the immediate attendance of any member absent without justifiable cause by designating a member of the Sanggunian, to be assisted by a member or members of the police force assigned in the territorial jurisdiction of the local government unit concerned, to arrest the absent member and present him at the session. (c) If there is still no quorum despite the enforcement of the immediately preceding subsection, no business shall be transacted. The presiding officer, upon proper motion duly approved by the members present, shall then declare the session adjourned for lack of quorum. While there is also no categorical statement in the aforequoted provisions of the Code requiring the physical presence of the sanggunian members to conduct a session, such physical presence can be inferred therefrom. While it is true that a work from home (WFH) arrangement is generally allowed pursuant to Civil Service Resolution No. 22002091, elective government officials are not covered, Item Ill thereof, states: Ill. SCOPE AND COVERAGE These policies shall apply to all appointive government officials and employees in all government agencies and instrumentalities, namely: Constitutional Bodies, departments, bureaus, and agencies of the National 1 Entitled, "POLICIES ON FLEXIBLE WORK ARRANGEMENTS IN THE GOVERNMENT", dated May 18, 2022 Page 2 of 3

Government; Government-Owned or-Controlled Corporations (GOCCs) with original charters; Local Government Units (LGUs); and State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), regardless of status of appointment (permanent, temporary, provisional, substitute, coterminous, casual, contractual or fixed term). With that, the Punong Barangay may be advised to file a leave of absence. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN TOR R.
